Source: step 0 of the parent proof ("If n > P, every n-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so S = 0; then S₀ := 0 satisfies (c) (both supports are empty, both densities are 0 everywhere) and (a), (b) are trivial"), with the details written out. Write d := dim L and m := n − d.
1. (Covectors of degree > P vanish.) Let k > P and α ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, k), a continuous alternating k-linear form on ℝ^P. For any v_1, …, v_k ∈ ℝ^P the family (v_i) is linearly dependent because k > P = dim ℝ^P, and an alternating multilinear map vanishes on every linearly dependent family (Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent, applied to α.toAlternatingMap). Hence α = 0.
2. (Currents of degree > P vanish.) Let U ⊆ ℝ^P and T ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with k > P. Every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k is a function with values in Covector(ℝ^P, k), so ω(x) = 0 for every x by step 1; hence ω is the zero element of the submodule TestFormOn U k and T ω = T 0 = 0 because T.toCurrent is linear. By extensionality (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), T = 0. In particular S = 0.
3. (Proof of (a) and (b).) For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ ≠ 0, blowUp S x λ is a current of degree n > P in dilation x λ '' univ, hence the zero current by step 2. By definition currentEval T ω equals either T⟨ω, h⟩ or 0; for T = blowUp S x λ both are 0. Since S ω = 0 as well, currentEval (blowUp S x λ h) ω = S ω for all x, λ ≠ 0, ω. Taking x = 0 and λ > 0 gives IsConeCurrent S; taking x = −v (v ∈ L) and λ = 1 gives (b).
4. (Zero currents.) Fix a degree j and let 0 ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ j.
(i) Mass: for every W, (0).massOn W = sSup {ofReal((0)(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ j W} = sSup {0} = 0; the set is exactly {0} because it is nonempty (the zero form is admissible: tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ W and its Euclidean norm is 0 ≤ 1).
(ii) Integer multiplicity: the triple R₀ with carrier ∅, mult ≡ 0 and orient ≡ 0 is an IMRep univ j: ∅ is Borel and contained in univ; it is countably j-rectifiable because H^j(∅) = 0 (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero); the constant multiplicity is measurable; mult_pos is vacuous; ∫⁻_{∅ ∩ K} mult dH^j = 0 ≠ ∞; the constant orientation is a.e. strongly measurable; the remaining a.e. condition refers to H^j⌞∅ = 0 and is vacuous. Its action is ∫_∅ (…) dH^j = 0 = (0)(ω) for every ω, so R₀ represents 0 and 0 is integer multiplicity.
(iii) Minimality: IsMinimizingIn 0 univ holds by (ii) and because (0).massOn W = 0 ≤ S'.massOn W for every competitor S' (by (i)).
(iv) Boundary: BoundaryVanishes 0 is True if j = 0; if j = j' + 1 then (0).boundary ω = (0)(dω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{j'}(ℝ^P), so (0).boundary = 0 by extensionality.
(v) Cone: for λ > 0, unfolding blowUp (restrictDomain followed by affinePushforward), every value of blowUp 0 0 λ is the zero current applied to a pulled-back test form, hence 0; so currentEval (blowUp 0 0 λ) ω = 0 = (0)(ω).
(vi) Support: (0).support = univ ∖ zeroRegion(0) = ∅. Indeed every x lies in the open ball B_1(x), whose closure B̄_1(x) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and contained in univ, and 0 vanishes on B_1(x); so x ∈ zeroRegion(0).
(vii) Densities: by (i) the quotient in HasMassDensity is 0 / (ω_j ρ^j) = 0 for every ρ (ENNReal.zero_div). As 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ and ℝ≥0∞ is Hausdorff, Tendsto (fun _ => 0) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (ofReal θ)) holds iff ofReal θ = 0, i.e. iff θ ≤ 0. Hence HasMassDensity 0 x θ ⟺ (0 ≤ θ ∧ θ ≤ 0) ⟺ θ = 0, for every x and every degree j.
5. (Proof of (c).) Put S₀ := 0 ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ m. By step 4 (iii)–(v), S₀ is minimizing in ℝ^P, BoundaryVanishes S₀ and S₀ is a cone. By (vi), spt S₀ = ∅ ⊆ L^⊥, and, since S = 0 (step 2), spt S = ∅ as well, so for t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥ both t + y ∈ spt S and y ∈ spt S₀ are false and hence equivalent. By (vii) applied in degrees n (to S = 0) and m (to S₀): HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ ⟺ θ = 0 ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ. Together with step 3 this proves (a), (b) and (c).
proof_key_steps: An alternating form of degree k > P on ℝ^P vanishes, so every test k-form is zero and every current of degree k > P is 0; hence S = 0 and all blow-ups of S are 0, giving (a) and (b).
The zero current of any degree has zero mass, is integer multiplicity via the empty IMRep, is minimizing, is a cycle and a cone, and has empty support.
For zero currents HasMassDensity x θ ⟺ θ = 0, so with S₀ := 0 both support and density equivalences of (c) hold.

Densities are unique: if HasMassDensity S x θ and HasMassDensity S x θ', the two limits along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0 in the Hausdorff space ℝ≥0∞ agree, so ofReal θ = ofReal θ', and θ, θ' ≥ 0 give θ = θ'. Consequently, for y ∈ L, λ > 0 and w ∈ ℝ^P, the hypothesis applied to HasMassDensity S w Θ(w) gives HasMassDensity S (y + λw) Θ(w), whence Θ(y + λw) = Θ(w).
2. (Preliminaries on μ.) μ = θ·H^n⌞M is a Borel measure, finite on compact sets (field locallyIntegrable_mult), hence outer regular. As θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ K) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for compact K, so ν := H^n⌞M is also locally finite, and μ and ν have the same null sets inside M. For r > 0 and x ∈ ℝ^P let η_{x,r}(z) := r^{−1}(z − x) (Chapter03.blowUpMap). H^n is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and H^n(cE) = c^n H^n(E) for c > 0 (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ / hausdorffMeasure_smul₀; equivalently the accepted DAG lemma euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables), so H^n(η_{x,r}(E)) = r^{−n} H^n(E).
3. (Θ = θ for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M.) Let G be the set of x ∈ M such that (α) M has an approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q; then dim Q = n), and (β) ν(B̄_ρ(x))^{−1} ∫_{M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)} |θ − θ(x)| dH^n → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. Property (α) holds for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M by the field orients of R. Property (β) holds for ν-a.e. x by the Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation theorem for the locally finite measure ν on ℝ^P and the locally ν-integrable function θ (Simon Ch. 1, §4; Mathlib Besicovitch.vitaliFamily with VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub, whose sets are closed balls centred at x). So H^n(M ∖ G) = 0. Fix x ∈ G.
(a) r^{−n} H^n(M ∩ B_r(x)) → ω_n as r ↓ 0. For ε ∈ (0, 1) choose continuous compactly supported f_−, f_+ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with f_− = 1 on B̄_{1−ε}(0), f_− = 0 off B_1(0), f_+ = 1 on B̄_1(0), f_+ = 0 off B_{1+ε}(0). Since η_{x,r}(M) ∩ B_1(0) = η_{x,r}(M ∩ B_r(x)), step 2 gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f_− dH^n ≤ r^{−n} H^n(M ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f_+ dH^n. By (α) the outer terms converge to ∫_Q f_∓ dH^n, which lie in [ω_n(1 − ε)^n, ω_n(1 + ε)^n] because H^n restricted to the n-dimensional subspace Q is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure (AffineSubspace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_coe_image; μHE[n] = volume on Euclid n), so H^n(Q ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n s^n. Letting ε ↓ 0 proves (a). The same argument with B̄ gives r^{−n} ν(B̄_r(x)) → ω_n.
(b) μ(B̄_ρ(x)) = ∫_{M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)} θ dH^n = θ(x) ν(B̄_ρ(x)) + e(ρ) with |e(ρ)| ≤ ∫_{M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)} |θ − θ(x)| dH^n = o(ν(B̄_ρ(x))) = o(ρ^n) by (β) and (a). Hence μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → θ(x). For every ε > 0, μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)), so the open-ball limit Θ(x) satisfies Θ(x) ≤ θ(x) ≤ (1 + ε)^n Θ(x); thus Θ(x) = θ(x).
4. (Θ = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∉ M.) Let t > 0, R' > 0 and A := {x ∈ B_{R'}(0) ∖ M : Θ(x) > t}. Then μ(A) = 0 because μ is concentrated on M. Let ε, δ ∈ (0, 1). By outer regularity there is an open U' ⊇ A with μ(U') < ε. For each x ∈ A, μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → Θ(x) > t, so there is ρ ∈ (0, δ) with B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ U' and μ(B_ρ(x)) > t ω_n ρ^n. By the Vitali 5r-covering lemma for closed balls of radii ≤ δ (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall) there is a countable pairwise disjoint subfamily (B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i)) with A ⊆ ⋃_i B̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i). Each B̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i) has diameter ≤ 10ρ_i ≤ 10δ, so the 10δ-approximating sum of the unnormalized Hausdorff measure μH[n] satisfies μH[n]_{10δ}(A) ≤ Σ_i (10ρ_i)^n ≤ 10^n (t ω_n)^{−1} Σ_i μ(B_{ρ_i}(x_i)) ≤ 10^n (t ω_n)^{−1} μ(U') ≤ 10^n ε/(t ω_n). Letting ε ↓ 0 and then δ ↓ 0 gives μH[n](A) = 0, hence H^n(A) = 0 since μHE[n] is a finite multiple of μH[n] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). Taking the union over R' ∈ ℕ and t = 1/k (k ∈ ℕ) shows H^n({x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0}) = 0.
5. (μ = Θ·H^n.) By steps 3 and 4 and Θ ≥ 0, ofReal ∘ Θ = θ·1_M H^n-a.e. Therefore for every Borel A, ∫_A ofReal Θ dH^n = ∫_{A ∩ M} θ dH^n = μ(A); i.e. μ(A) = (H^n.withDensity (ofReal ∘ Θ))(A).
6. (Translation invariance, (i).) Let y ∈ L and A Borel; (fun x => y + x)⁻¹' A = A − y. The map z ↦ z + y is an isometry of ℝ^P, so it preserves H^n (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). By step 1 applied with the vector −y ∈ L and λ = 1, Θ((−y) + 1·x) = Θ(x) for every x, i.e. Θ(x − y) = Θ(x). Using step 5 and the change of variables x = z + y: μ(A − y) = ∫_{A − y} ofReal Θ(z) dH^n(z) = ∫_A ofReal Θ(x − y) dH^n(x) = ∫_A ofReal Θ(x) dH^n(x) = μ(A).
7. (Homogeneity, (ii).) Let λ > 0 and A Borel; λA = (fun x => λ • x) '' A is Borel (image under a homeomorphism). By step 2, for every Borel g ≥ 0, ∫_{λA} g dH^n = λ^n ∫_A g(λw) dH^n(w): the image of the measure H^n⌞A under w ↦ λw is λ^{−n}·H^n⌞(λA), because H^n(A ∩ λ^{−1}E) = λ^{−n} H^n(λA ∩ E) (H^n(λF) = λ^n H^n(F) for every F) (the accepted DAG lemma euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables states this change of variables). By step 1 with y = 0 ∈ L, Θ(λw) = Θ(w). Hence, by step 5, μ(λA) = ∫_{λA} ofReal Θ dH^n = λ^n ∫_A ofReal Θ(λw) dH^n(w) = λ^n ∫_A ofReal Θ dH^n = λ^n μ(A), i.e. μ((fun x => λ • x) '' A) = ofReal(λ^n)·μ(A).
(If P < n then H^n = 0 on ℝ^P, μ = 0 and (i), (ii) hold trivially; the argument above covers this case as well.)

At H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (approximate tangent space and Besicovitch–Lebesgue point of θ) the density is θ(x); hence Θ = θ a.e. on M.

1. (Pointwise duality.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let α be an n-covector. By multilinearity and alternation, α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where τ^I is the n × n matrix (⟨e_{i_a}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = det(I_n) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, with equality for α_τ := Σ_I det(τ^I) dx^I, which satisfies |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1. (For n = 0 both sides equal |α()| and α_τ := 1.)

By the field `orients` of IMRep, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ(x) and a sign σ(x) ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(τ(x)) for every n-covector α (IsUnitOrientationOf). For all large j, γ_j is C^∞, tsupport γ_j is a compact subset of V ⊆ W ⊆ U, |γ_j| ≤ 1 everywhere (Jensen's inequality for the convex function |·|), and γ_j → γ uniformly. On K', ξ(γ) = ξ(β) = 1 μ_R-a.e.; on V ∖ K', |ξ(γ)| ≤ 1; off V, γ = 0. Hence ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(V ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − ε) − 2ε, since μ_R(V ∖ K') ≤ μ_R(V ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K') < 2ε. By the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on such a generating π-system, R'.measure(A ∩ U) = R.measure(A ∩ U) for every Borel A, hence R'.measure = R.measure.

The restriction of p to T_x is the orthogonal projection of T_x onto L ⊆ T_x, so the coarea Jacobian J^M p(x) equals 1. For an integer multiplicity current A supported in L^⊥ with tangent planes in L^⊥, A(ω♭(t + ·)) = ϕ(t) A(β) (on L^⊥, q = id and Λ^m q is the identity on m-vectors of L^⊥; compute with a representation of A).
